meaning.en: Success or failure, favourable or unfavourable outcomes: all the possible results of an undertaking.
meaning.zh: 指事情的成功或失败、顺利或不顺利。

equivalents: the ups and downs of the outcome

examples.zh: 我们尽力而为，至于成败利钝，就不必多想了。
examples.en: We will do our best; as for success or failure, there is no need to dwell on it.

examples.zh: 他把个人的成败利钝置之度外，一心推进改革。
examples.en: Setting personal gain and loss aside, he devoted himself to pushing the reform through.

story.en: Zhuge Liang, explaining why he would still march north: 'As for success or failure, favourable or not, that is beyond my foresight' (至于成败利钝，非臣之明所能逆睹也).
story.zh: 诸葛亮《后出师表》：“臣鞠躬尽瘁，死而后已。至于成败利钝，非臣之明所能逆睹也。”

date.zh: 三国蜀汉 · 传为228年（真伪存疑）

usage.en: Literary; usually in the pattern '至于成败利钝' or '不计成败利钝' to say one will do one's duty whatever the outcome. 钝 here means 'unfavourable'.
usage.zh: 书面语，常说“至于成败利钝”“不计成败利钝”，表示尽力而为、不问结果。“钝”指不顺利。

meaning.en: Acknowledging neither parent nor ruler; utterly lacking in filial piety and loyalty, defying all authority.
meaning.zh: 目无尊长，不讲孝道，不忠于君主，形容人毫无礼法、狂悖放肆。

equivalents: with no respect for parent or ruler

examples.zh: 在旧时人看来，他离家出走、不认宗族，简直是无父无君。
examples.en: In the eyes of people of the old days, leaving home and disowning his clan made him utterly disrespectful of all authority.

examples.zh: 保守的族长骂这个年轻人无父无君。
examples.en: The conservative clan elder cursed the young man for respecting neither father nor ruler.

story.en: Mencius condemned the schools of Yang Zhu and Mo Di: 'Yang denies the ruler, Mo denies the father; to have no father and no ruler is to be a beast' (无父无君，是禽兽也).
story.zh: 《孟子》：“杨氏为我，是无君也；墨氏兼爱，是无父也。无父无君，是禽兽也。”

usage.en: Strongly condemnatory and now dated; belongs to the language of traditional Confucian ethics. Today used mostly in historical contexts or half-jokingly.
usage.zh: 贬义，语气很重，带有传统儒家伦理色彩，现多用于历史语境或戏谑。

meaning.en: To do as one wishes; at its best, to act freely and naturally without ever breaking the rules.
meaning.zh: 随着自己的心意，想怎么做就怎么做。

examples.zh: 孔子说到七十岁才能从心所欲，不逾矩。
examples.en: Confucius said that only at seventy could he follow his heart's desires without overstepping the line.

examples.zh: 退休以后，他终于可以从心所欲地旅行、读书。
examples.en: After retiring, he could at last travel and read just as he pleased.

story.en: Confucius summed up his life: 'At seventy I could follow my heart's desires without overstepping the line' (七十而从心所欲，不逾矩).
story.zh: 《论语·为政》：“七十而从心所欲，不逾矩。”

usage.en: Neutral or positive in the Confucian sense (freedom within the rules); in loose use it can sound self-indulgent. The classic line pairs it with 不逾矩. 七十 is called 从心之年 for this reason.
usage.zh: 在儒家语境中是褒义（自由而不越规矩），泛用时也可含放纵意味。原文与“不逾矩”相连，七十岁因此称“从心之年”。

natural: drive the sparrows into the thicket

meaning.en: To drive the very people you want to keep into the arms of your rival by treating them badly.
meaning.zh: 把鸟雀赶到丛林里去，比喻不会团结人，把本可争取的人推到对方那边去。

equivalents: drive people into the enemy's camp
push allies over to the other side

examples.zh: 对员工动辄训斥，只会为丛驱雀，把人才都赶到竞争对手那里。
examples.en: Constantly berating staff only drives talent into the competition's arms.

examples.zh: 他不会团结同学，反而为丛驱雀，让朋友越来越少。
examples.en: He could not draw classmates together; instead he drove them away and had ever fewer friends.

story.en: Mencius: 'The one who drives the fish into the deep is the otter; the one who drives the sparrows into the thicket is the hawk' (为渊驱鱼者，獭也；为丛驱爵者，鹯也).
story.zh: 《孟子》：“为渊驱鱼者，獭也；为丛驱爵者，鹯也；为汤武驱民者，桀与纣也。”

usage.en: Literary and rare; the image is a hawk that chases sparrows into the bushes. Often paired with 为渊驱鱼. Critical in tone.
usage.zh: 书面语，较少见；比喻像鹞子把雀赶进丛林。常与“为渊驱鱼”并提，带批评意味。

meaning.en: A skill or talent equal to ten thousand enemies; by extension, great military or strategic ability.
meaning.zh: 能抵挡万人的本领，指军事、谋略上的大才。

equivalents: a match for an entire army

examples.zh: 项羽说学剑只能敌一人，要学就学万人之敌。
examples.en: Xiang Yu said that swordsmanship beats only one man; he wanted to learn how to take on ten thousand.

examples.zh: 他自幼读兵书，立志成为万人之敌。
examples.en: From boyhood he read books on war, resolved to become a match for ten thousand.

story.en: Xiang Yu gave up swordsmanship as 'good only against one man' and said he would learn the art to 'match ten thousand' (学万人敌).
story.zh: 《史记·项羽本纪》：“剑一人敌，不足学，学万人敌。”

usage.en: Literary, praising. In modern writing it can describe an outstanding strategist or champion, and is occasionally used humorously.
usage.zh: 书面语，褒义，现代可形容杰出的统帅或高手，偶有戏谑用法。

literal: call oneself · the Solitary · speak of oneself as · the Lone

meaning.en: To call oneself 'the Solitary One' and 'the Lone One' as kings did; hence to set oneself up as ruler or boss.
meaning.zh: 古代君主自称“孤”“寡人”，比喻自立为王，或自以为是、独断专行。

examples.zh: 他刚坐上经理的位置就在部门里称孤道寡。
examples.en: No sooner had he become manager than he began lording it over the department.

examples.zh: 乱世中，各路军阀纷纷称孤道寡。
examples.en: In the chaos, warlords of every stripe styled themselves kings.

usage.en: Mostly derogatory, either for rebels who proclaim themselves rulers or for people who act like petty tyrants. 孤 and 寡 were humble royal self-references.
usage.zh: 多含贬义，指割据称王，或比喻在小范围内自封霸主。“孤”“寡”本是君主的谦称。

meaning.en: Small and scattered here and there, like stars or specks.
meaning.zh: 形容细小而分散的东西，到处都有一点儿。

examples.zh: 山坡上星星点点开满了野花。
examples.en: Wild flowers dotted the hillside here and there.

examples.zh: 夜里的渔火星星点点，映在湖面上。
examples.en: The fishing lights twinkled in scattered points, reflected on the lake.

usage.en: Descriptive, often in scenery writing; usually an adverbial or attributive. Can also mean 'tiny bits' (星星点点的收获).
usage.zh: 描写景物常用，多作状语、定语，也可表示少量零碎的东西。

meaning.en: To roam far from home making a living by one's wits and skills, gaining experience of the world.
meaning.zh: 离开家乡，在外面四处奔走谋生，见识社会。

equivalents: make one's way in the wide world

examples.zh: 他十六岁就出门闯荡江湖，什么苦都吃过。
examples.en: He set out to make his own way at sixteen and has known every hardship.

examples.zh: 爷爷年轻时闯荡江湖，卖过艺也当过伙计。
examples.en: In his youth grandfather roamed the country, once performing in the street and once clerking in a shop.

usage.en: Originally about wandering martial artists and performers; now used widely for anyone striking out on their own. Casual and slightly romantic.
usage.zh: 原指武林人士、艺人漂泊谋生，现泛指在外独自打拼。口语，略带传奇色彩。

meaning.en: Getting more serious with every passing day; used mainly of bad things growing worse.
meaning.zh: 一天比一天厉害，多指不好的情况越来越严重。

examples.zh: 环境污染日甚一日，必须尽快治理。
examples.en: Pollution is getting worse by the day and must be tackled quickly.

examples.zh: 他的思乡之情日甚一日。
examples.en: His homesickness grew stronger every day.

usage.en: Usually about negative things (illness, pollution, longing); predicate or adverbial. For neutral growth use 与日俱增.
usage.zh: 多用于不好的事物（病情、污染、思念等），作谓语或状语。中性的增长多用“与日俱增”。

meaning.en: To keep saying 'yes, yes' in a servile or agreeable manner, without objecting to anything.
meaning.zh: 连连答应“是是”，形容一味顺从、不敢反驳的样子。

examples.zh: 面对上司的责骂，他只是诺诺连声。
examples.en: Faced with his boss's scolding, he just kept saying 'yes, yes'.

examples.zh: 店员诺诺连声地答应了客人所有要求。
examples.en: The shop assistant fawningly agreed to all the customer's demands.

usage.en: Mildly derogatory: it suggests meekness or sycophancy. Often paired with 唯唯诺诺. Predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 略含贬义，带有唯唯诺诺、畏缩顺从之意，多作谓语或状语。

meaning.en: Impossible to put into words; too deep or subtle to express.
meaning.zh: 无法用言语表达，指感受或道理极其深刻、微妙。

examples.zh: 站在山顶的那份喜悦，实在不可言喻。
examples.en: The joy of standing on the summit was beyond words.

examples.zh: 两人之间有一种不可言喻的默契。
examples.en: There was an unspoken understanding between the two.

usage.en: Positive or neutral; attributive or predicate. Close to 不可名状 and 难以言表; 喻 here means 'to explain'. Note: do not write 不可言谕.
usage.zh: 可褒可中性，作定语或谓语。与“不可名状”“难以言表”相近；“喻”意为说明，不要写成“谕”。

meaning.en: Pain or hatred so intense that it seems to go into the bone marrow.
meaning.zh: 痛苦或痛恨深入骨髓，形容极其深切。

equivalents: hatred that cuts to the bone

examples.zh: 国破家亡的惨痛让他痛入骨髓。
examples.en: The anguish of a ruined country and family cut him to the bone.

examples.zh: 她对骗子恨得痛入骨髓。
examples.en: She hated the swindler to the very marrow.

usage.en: Describes physical pain, grief or hatred; literary, predicate. Compare 恨之入骨 (hatred only).
usage.zh: 可指肉体痛苦、悲痛或仇恨，书面语，多作谓语。与“恨之入骨”相比，后者只指仇恨。

meaning.en: To feel vaguely that something is missing, with a sense of emptiness.
meaning.zh: 好像丢了什么东西似的，形容心里空落落的。

equivalents: feel as if something is missing

examples.zh: 毕业典礼之后，他总觉得若有所失。
examples.en: After graduation he always felt as if something were missing.

examples.zh: 儿子上了大学，母亲整天若有所失。
examples.en: With her son away at university, the mother went about all day feeling something was gone.

usage.en: Commonly a predicate or adverbial. Milder and more ordinary than 茫然若失 and often about departures or endings.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语。比“茫然若失”平和日常，常用于离别或结束之后。

meaning.en: Thousands upon thousands of households; also the many gates and doors of a great palace.
meaning.zh: 形容住户众多，也形容宫殿、建筑群的门户重重。

equivalents: a maze of gates and halls

examples.zh: 除夕之夜，千门万户灯火通明。
examples.en: On New Year's Eve, lights blazed in countless homes.

examples.zh: 站在山上俯瞰古城，千门万户尽收眼底。
examples.en: From the hill one could take in the whole old city, its myriad houses spread below.

story.en: Wang Anshi's New Year poem speaks of 'ten thousand gates and thousand doors, always the new peach charms replacing the old' (千门万户曈曈日，总把新桃换旧符).
story.zh: 王安石《元日》：“千门万户曈曈日，总把新桃换旧符。”

usage.en: Poetic, with a warm tone; commonly used in scene-setting about cities and festivals. Compare 万家灯火.
usage.zh: 带诗意，常用来写城市、节日的景象。可比较“万家灯火”。

meaning.en: Astonishment and joy together, usually on receiving unexpected good news.
meaning.zh: 又吃惊又高兴，多指突然遇到好事时的复杂心情。

examples.zh: 收到录取通知书，她惊喜交加，说不出话来。
examples.en: On receiving the admission letter she was speechless with surprised delight.

examples.zh: 看到失散多年的老友，他惊喜交加。
examples.en: Seeing an old friend lost for years, he was surprised and overjoyed.

usage.en: Describes a reaction to a good surprise; predicate or adverbial. Compare 悲喜交加 (grief and joy).
usage.zh: 描写意外之喜的反应，作谓语或状语。可比较“悲喜交加”。
